payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_home_lock.py::test_a_batch_beside_a_live_task_leaves_it_in_its_state stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/cli.py. The claim was 'A batch started beside a live task leaves that task in its in-flight state, and stamps nothing `ORPHANED`. The witness drives one live task per holder. A running batch holds a task in `REVIEWING`, a running cell one in `IMPLEMENTING`, and a running draft one in `QUEUED`. The second batch is the real `_batch`, whose scan would stamp each one.'. Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_cli.py::test_the_batch_scan_asks_for_the_stamping_the_attended_one_refuses, tests/test_cli.py::test_the_batch_rescans_through_the_pinned_base_without_stamping_orphans, tests/test_cli.py::test_the_batch_scan_orphans_the_queue_row_of_each_task_it_stamps, tests/test_cli.py::test_saffron_batch_stack_plans_once_and_runs_that_order, tests/test_home_lock.py::test_a_killed_holder_frees_the_home_and_its_row_is_stamped_orphaned, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
